span.term: Judgments about possible laws are generated from a prototype or essentialized concept of law, assembled from simpler concepts such as norm, fairness and punishment, that is only weakly tied to experience of actual laws

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Asking about possible rather than actual laws shifts attention from surface features to the deeper criteria for category membership, such as the purpose or moral dimension of law
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Prescriptive reasoning bleeds into descriptive judgment: asked whether laws necessarily have a property, participants also weigh whether that property is desirable — a mechanism the paper proposes and then partly disconfirms
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The study documents the effect but not the cognitive mechanism producing the contradictory beliefs.
span.note: what this limits: any mechanistic reading: OUR STUDY ... AFFORDED LIMITED INSIGHT INTO THE PSYCHOLOGICAL PROCESSES THAT ENGENDER CONFLICTING BELIEFS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Prescriptive thinking was measured only by explicit self-report, leaving unconscious routes untested.
span.note: what this limits: the prescriptive-thinking measure: WE ASSESSED PARTICIPANTS' ENGAGEMENT IN PRESCRIPTIVE THINKING THROUGH THEIR EXPLICIT REPORTS, [which] LEAVES OPEN UNCONSCIOUS PATHWAYS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Effect size varied substantially by country, which may indicate cultural variability or sampling differences.
span.note: what this limits: the cross-cultural generality claim: THE MAGNITUDE OF THE EFFECT VARIED SUBSTANTIALLY ACROSS COUNTRIES, WHICH MAY IMPLY SOME DEGREE OF CULTURAL VARIABILITY - or sampling differences, and the study cannot choose
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect is documented but its mechanism is not: the study is stated to give limited insight into the processes that produce the conflicting beliefs.
span.note: what this limits: explaining WHY people hold both beliefs: the authors state the study evidences the phenomenon but gives limited insight into the psychological processes producing it
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Only explicit reports of prescriptive thinking were measured, so an unconscious route from moral considerations to judgements of possibility remains open by the authors' own statement.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that the effect is not moral in origin: the authors rule this out only for prescriptive thinking that participants could report, and say so
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The cross-country variation in effect size cannot be attributed: culture and sampling method are confounded, because recruitment differed substantially across sites.
span.note: what this limits: reading the country differences as cultural variability: the authors state sampling methods differed substantially across sites, so the variation might instead reflect sample composition or acquiescence
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two-way classification of legal systems used to select sites is reported by the authors as sometimes seen as too coarse.
span.note: what this limits: the common-law versus civil-law contrast as the axis of cross-cultural comparison: the paper notes the distinction is sometimes seen as overly coarse
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The per-site sample target was not met everywhere.
span.note: what this limits: per-country estimates: the stated minimum of 100 per condition per site was met everywhere except Cambodia
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across 11 countries people simultaneously held two inconsistent beliefs: that laws violating procedural principles could not exist, and that such laws in fact do exist.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Participants asked about actual laws said those laws violate the procedural principles about half the time, whereas participants asked about possible laws overwhelmingly denied that the same principles could be violated.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The modal-versus-existential effect appeared separately in every one of the 11 countries sampled.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect also held separately for each of the eight procedural principles tested.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The size of the effect nevertheless differed by country, being weakest in India and the United Kingdom and strongest in Brazil and Poland.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The size of the effect also differed by principle, being smallest for the generality principle and largest for the consistency principle.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A post-test showed the manipulation worked as intended on the existential side: the 'There are laws' wording was read as a question about what laws are usually like in the respondent's experience.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The modal wording, however, was read in two ways at once — as asking what laws must be like to count as law, and as asking what laws ideally should be like.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect survived among the minority who read the modal purely as a question of necessity rather than of what ought to be, which rules out the explanation that the paradox is an artifact of deontic reading.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The pattern was equally present across age groups, genders, and between lawyers and non-lawyers.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: People believe laws necessarily cannot punish past conduct retroactively, be kept secret, or be incomprehensible, while also acknowledging that real laws break exactly these constraints.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
